Our Mission
Through understanding the unique nature of each child, our aim is to inspire children to become creative, independent thinkers, competent communicators and to build positive relationships. We wish them to care for the world around them and be happy, confident, enquiring individuals who love to learn and contribute to their school and other communities.

About Us
Headteacher's Welcome
A warm welcome to the Children’s House. I’m very proud of our school. For over 50 years, the school has prioritised families and children, emphasising individualised learning. We are an exceptionally happy school, and have become known for nurturing children to become confident, creative, independent thinkers.
Our ethos is based on high teacher-to-child ratios and small class sizes. This allows us to spend more time with each child, ensuring they get the maximum out of their critical early learning years. We have a full-time SENCo on site, supported by a team of specialists who support children in all areas, from social emotional learning to phonics and maths.
Teaching the expected curriculum and achieving excellence in exams is important (and our results are excellent) but we believe that learning has to be fun and engaging. With this in mind, we’ve developed Theme-based Learning throughout the school, tying together the traditional subjects, developing depth of understanding and inspiring stronger, cross-subject interest.
At both sites, sports, outdoor time and before and after-school clubs play an important part of the day. We have weekly PE that includes swimming, dance and a wide variety of other sports. The Prep school children play sports fixtures against other schools and enrichment activities range from Chess to Fencing to LAMDA to Choir, allowing each child to develop a wide range of hobbies and interests.
I’d welcome the opportunity to show you around the school; we believe that we have something very special here.

About Us
Our History and Ethos
Our History and Ethos
The Children’s House was set up in 1973 by a group of local parents, to provide high-quality early years education in Islington. It was originally run in a parent’s home and then in St Stephen’s Church in Canonbury Road. Parents wanted to build on the Nursery provision and in 2005 we leased a Victorian school building on King Henry’s Walk and opened the Prep School. In 2026, we purchased a new purpose-built school building on Kingsbury Road, just seconds from the Prep School, and from 2027 we will move our Early Years pupils to King Henry's Walk and Prep pupils to the new, larger site.
Our present-day Early Years Site in Elmore Street caters for children ranging in age from 2½ to 5 years. The Prep School is on King Henry’s Walk a 15-minute walk away and caters for pupils from Year 1 to Year 6.
The Early Years Site consists of two enormous open-plan rooms; one downstairs for our Reception class and one upstairs for Nursery and Pre-Reception classes. The children belong to small classes with a teacher and a teaching assistant. As well as a wide range of activities and learning opportunities in the school, they enjoy a variety of weekly outings, which provide regular access to outdoor learning. These venues vary throughout the year and include the Almorah Community Garden, King Henry’s Walk Community Garden, soft play at Queensbridge Leisure Centre and the Prep School playground.
The Prep School has six light-filled classrooms which surround an enclosed astro-turfed playground. We have an all-weather pitch and Adventure playground close to the school and also use nearby leisure centres for sports and PE.

About Us
About Us
We are a co-educational, nursery to 11+ private school in North London (N1) helping children develop a love of learning and become strong creative, independent thinkers.
We focus on theme-based learning techniques, tying the traditional curriculum subjects together, developing depth of understanding and inspiring stronger, cross-subject interest and independent thinking. This makes learning fun, meaningful and creative.
We take children of all abilities and with small class sizes and excellent, highly qualified teachers, they excel. Our school isn’t just about achieving outstanding academic results, it’s about building confident, well-rounded, happy children.

Kindness * Curiosity * Calm
OUR EDUCATIONAL AIMS FOR EACH CHILD:
By Summer 2028, The Children’s House will be a desirable and well-recognised Prep School, both locally amongst nurseries, and amongst the wider London independent day school community. We will be recognised for delivering exceptional academic progress and high value-added outcomes, ensuring every learner, regardless of background or ability has the opportunity to thrive. We will be known as a School that prioritises personal development, fostering kindness, creativity, independence and critical thinking. Pupils will leave at 11+ well prepared for the next stage of their academic journey as confident communicators and caring citizens. Staff will be highly equipped to tailor teaching to individual needs and nurture calm and creativity in all pupils.

Early Years
Early Years
Special Educational Needs
"The SENCo – notably, also the school’s mental health lead - is ‘outstanding’ and ‘a fantastic addition’" ~ GOOD SCHOOLS GUIDE 2023
We place a strong emphasis on supporting every child from their earliest years and believe that early identification and intervention are key to unlocking each child's full potential.
Our SENCo, Laura, who is also our More Able and Mental Health Lead, plays a crucial role in coordinating individualised learning interventions. In these roles, she ensures that all children, from their earliest days in our care, receive the support and challenges they need, while prioritising their overall wellbeing.
In the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), we offer targeted interventions to help children develop essential skills in areas like communication and language, physical development and personal, social and emotional development. These early interventions are collaborative, involving close communication between teachers, parents, and external professionals when needed, to ensure that support is consistent at school and at home. By setting individualised targets that are reviewed termly, we ensure that every child has the opportunity to make steady progress, whether they need a short-term boost or more sustained support.
Our approach to identifying and nurturing more able students also begins in the early years. Our staff are trained to recognise exceptional potential in academic subjects, sports, or the arts, and to provide additional challenges and enrichment opportunities from the start. This ensures that all children have the chance to excel in areas of strength. For more able pupils, individualised targets are set, and they are supported with tailored tasks that stretch their abilities. We also teach them valuable meta-cognitive strategies, helping them become aware of their strengths and how to harness them for future success.
By focusing on early intervention and personalised learning from the beginning, we ensure that every child at The Children's House is given the best possible start on their educational journey.
Cookie Policy

pageCache.text:
Parents
Before and After School Clubs
Before and After School Clubs
At The Children’s House, the school day doesn’t simply begin and end at the classroom door. Our before and after‑school clubs are a valued part of school life, offering children the chance to explore interests, build friendships and enjoy a relaxed, happy start and finish to each day. From breakfast club and gentle morning activities to a vibrant programme of enrichment after school, children are supported by familiar staff in a caring, welcoming environment.
Our after‑school programme offers something for everyone, with a broad mix of creative, practical, academic and active clubs across the week. Children might be found creating art or pottery, performing drama, coding, gardening, playing sport, or discovering new talents through music and movement. Alongside enrichment, we provide reliable after‑school and extended care, giving families flexibility and reassurance. Parents value knowing that their children are not only well cared for, but genuinely enjoying their time at school right through to pick‑up.
Please contact the office to arrange a login to Scopay where you can access ad hoc club bookings, extended care and enrichment clubs.
Cookie Policy

Prep School
Prep School
Curriculum
In Reception, we continue to follow the Early Years Foundation Stage. More information can be found on our Nursery pages.
In Key Stages 1 and 2, we follow the National Curriculum and prepare children for the 11+. More details can be found below by subject.
Information & Communication Technology
Personal Health and Social Education
Subjects are taught through topics. Foundation subjects and Science are taught in blocks so that children can immerse themselves in the topics. Topics are linked through an overarching ‘umbrella’ theme to enable children to make connections across the curriculum and to experience breadth and depth in their learning.
Personal Health and Social Education
In Circle Time, assemblies and throughout each day, we talk to children about important issues, for example, keeping safe and healthy, caring for living things, how to be a good friend.
Specialist Teaching
Children have weekly PE sessions with a specialist PE teacher. Dance, swimming, tennis and athletics are rotated with traditional team sports and skills activities to ensure pupils experience a wide variety of physical education.
Children are taught computing skills one-to-one and in groups with our ICT teacher using Chromebooks. They are also taught about online and cyber security in an age appropriate way.
Our Spanish teacher uses games, stories, songs, rhymes and role play to introduce the children to Spanish words and phrases.
Younger pupils learn singing and rhythm with our Music teacher and older children may learn recorder or ukulele in their class, depending on their age and the curriculum for their year group. We also provide individual piano, flute, ukulele and guitar lessons for those who are interested in learning an instrument.
Cookie Policy

Prep School
Prep School
SEND & More Able Provision
"The SENCo – notably, also the school’s mental health lead - is ‘outstanding’ and ‘a fantastic addition’" ~ GOOD SCHOOLS GUIDE 2023
At The Children's House, we provide a holistic approach to individualised learning, and our SENCo, Laura, is also our More Able and Mental Health Lead.
In these three roles, she coordinates the individualised interventions provided to both support and challenge pupils, and has oversight for the wellbeing of all pupils.
Pupils with Special Educational Needs may be offered targeted interventions in a wide range of areas, ranging from fine and gross motor skills, handwriting, emotional resilience to problem-solving in Maths. Sometimes, these SEN interventions are short term, providing a little boost to build confidence or plug a knowledge gap, and in other situations may be longer lasting. Laura works collaboratively with teachers and parents to create targets for pupils and reviews these each term.
On the More Able front, we are always looking to identify potential or capacity for high attainment in a particular area, be this academic, sport or the arts and are committed to nurturing and championing these strengths. Whilst our teachers implement challenges for all students across the curriculum, More Able pupils will be set individualised targets and offered more tailored stretch and challenge tasks. We also encourage our More Able students to become more aware of their potential using a range of meta-cognitive strategies, allowing them to truly flourish.
“The support Laura (SENCo) has provided for my daughter has completely transformed her. With Laura’s guidance, we devised a program to build her confidence. Laura approaches her work with understanding, kindness and patience. My daughter loves her and I am thrilled with all the success.”
Cookie Policy

Early Years
Early Years
Early Years
A First Step in nurturing confident, creative, independent thinkers
Most children begin their educational journey at The Children’s House in the Early Years, joining from the age of two and a half.
In the first term, they attend the Early Years School, with the initial half-term focused on settling in and immersing into the school routine. We encourage and support their continuous engagement in a full day of activities. At the beginning of the year in which they turn four, children then transition to the pre-reception class.
All Early Years children benefit from being in small classes led by a qualified teacher and a teaching assistant. The school maintains high adult/child ratios, facilitating constant observation and interaction. This allows the staff to know the children well and provide individualised learning experiences throughout their school journey.
Children begin each morning and afternoon session with their teacher and enjoy a whole-class learning focus together. Related activities are set up on tables. Children access a full range of practical activities, from role-play to writing. Whatever the learning focus, we ensure learning is enjoyable, creative and hands-on.
Specialist teachers visit the Early Years School to deliver lessons in Spanish and dance. We also bring a range of visitors into the school to deliver storytelling, puppet shows, drumming, animal workshops amongst other things. Children are given regular outdoor experiences through timetabled visits to Almorah Gardens, King Henry’s Walk Community Garden and the Prep School playground.

The School has a bursarial fund available for pupils in all year groups. Bursary places are offered on the basis of a means test by an external agency. If you would like to enquire about bursary places please contact Admissions on admissions@childrenshouseschool.co.uk.
Bursary and Hardship Policy
Early Education Funding
The government introduced revised Early Years funding (previously Nursery Education Grant Scheme) from September 2025, and we continue to participate in this scheme. Please note that our provision starts for pupils from 2 years of age.
The funding only covers basic care and falls well below our standard fees for a broad educational “school” experience. Our commitment is to provide a high-quality education that supports every child’s full development in readiness for our Prep School. This includes a vibrant curriculum taught by qualified teachers, plus a rich programme of sports, Spanish, music and dance led by specialist teachers. Children also benefit from external trips and are offered enrichment clubs, all of which are central to helping our pupils grow into confident, independent learners.
Our Early Years setting is open for 36 weeks of the year. Government-funded childcare hours are allocated over 38 weeks, and we do not currently offer a stretched entitlement. This means that any funded hours not used during our term-time provision may be claimed at another eligible setting. If you would like further information about your funding entitlement or have any questions about accessing your remaining funded hours, please contact Nicolette (admissions@childrenshouseschool.co.uk), who will be happy to help.
15 hours – All children from 3 years of age
For children aged over 3 years of age, the government funds 15 hours per week, irrespective of family income. We offer these hours from 12 - 3pm Monday to Friday. Children whose parents meet the financial eligibility criteria may also benefit from the additional 15 hours per week. We offer these hours from 3 – 6pm.
30 hours – for eligible children from 2 years of age
Government funding requires both parents to earn over £167 per week but under £100,000 annually. If either parent falls outside this range, the family is ineligible. Eligibility for the extended entitlement is determined by HMRC. Parents must apply through the Government’s Best Start in Life portal and provide a valid code before the start of each funded term. More information can be found here.
Applications must be submitted on the government site and the child’s code sent to us by 31 July, 30 November, or 31 March for the following term. Codes must be renewed each term, and missed deadlines mean waiting until the next cycle—there is no flexibility for new starters.
For eligible families, we provide these fully funded places for 30 hours per week from 12-6pm from Monday - Friday, for 36 weeks a year, following our academic terms.
Morning sessions (8:45 am – 12:00 pm), extra-curricular and enrichment activities are not included in the funding.
All new admissions places are subject to availability and are considered in line with our Admissions Policy. The School’s Terms and Conditions will apply.
